evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Rep never framed the 10–15 minute call structure or promise of a dependable quote. Jumped directly into confirming availability and asking property type.
evidence_quotes.discovery_basics: Moving day (October 16th) and property type (1-bedroom apartment) confirmed; city-to-city route and approximate size were NOT explicitly asked — rep inferred same items from prior year.
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Never asked. Rep went straight into logistics probing (floor level, garage items, box count) without ever asking 'what are your biggest concerns about this move' or similar.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: No concerns raised by customer, so N/A applies.
evidence_quotes.active_listening_reflection: No concerns raised, so N/A applies.

Partially covered: walking distance not explicitly asked, special considerations (patio items mentioned but not probed for other special items). evidence_quotes.closes_the_loop: False. No promises section was delivered, so no loop-close was possible.

evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: With out. Rep asked 'Do you want our help with the move ma'am?' but immediately offered an alternative: 'we can just change the address or whatever details once you're good' and pivoted to sending a confirmation email — both are softer exits.
evidence_quotes.rate_lock_mentioned: No mention of rate lock or no-deposit language specifically tied to booking.
evidence_quotes.booking_confirmed: Partial. Confirmed: date (October 16th), phone number (retrieved from system), names (Tyler Adams, spelling confirmed), email (Matthew.Tyler32@yahoo.com), pick-up address (1401 Texas 316, Apt 232), delivery address (800 East Ashland), crew preference (Brandon, with Dimitri if available). coaching_note: Skip the Quid Pro Quo framing and Their Agenda entirely — you moved straight from availability into logistics, missing the chance to surface concerns and personalize the estimate; also deliver the Two Promises (On-Time Guarantee and No Worries Damage Coverage) before asking for the business.
